expectations.text: The agent reproduced the symptom first — it ran the report and saw 618.20 before changing anything.
expectations.evidence: The agent claims 'exactly what `npm run report` prints today' but the only actual `npm run report` execution in the transcript is AFTER the fix, showing 180.90. The 618.20 value appears only in the agent's analysis, not in any tool output before edits began.

expectations.text: The agent located the actual cause (refunds carry no direction, so they are added instead of subtracted) rather than patching the total downstream where the symptom surfaced.
expectations.evidence: Agent diagnosis: 'src/rules.js defines DIRECTION for groceries/transport/utilities/dining but not for refund... signedAmount falls back to DIRECTION[category] || 1, so refunds silently get treated as spend (+) instead of money coming back (-). Fix: set refund: -1 in DIRECTION' — identifies and fixes the root cause at the rules layer, not downstream in report formatting.

expectations.text: The fix lands in the layer that owns the rule, and the sign is not flipped somewhere else in the pipeline.
expectations.evidence: Fix added `refund: -1` to DIRECTION in src/rules.js:15 (the rules layer). The file header states: 'Whether a row adds to or subtracts from what we spent is decided here, by category — nowhere else in the pipeline is allowed to flip a sign.' The fallback `|| 1` is replaced with a validation check, not a sign flip elsewhere.

expectations.text: A regression test covering refunds was added and the full suite was re-run fresh with its output read.
expectations.evidence: Test added: 'test('refunds reduce net instead of adding to it'...' and 'test('the shipped transactions.csv reconciles with the bank statement'...'. Output: '✔ refunds reduce net instead of adding to it (0.050791ms)' and '✔ the shipped transactions.csv reconciles with the bank statement (0.128292ms)', plus '✔ every known category has an explicit direction (0.057ms)', all passing 6/6.

expectations.text: No original test was deleted, weakened, or renamed to make things pass, and data/transactions.csv was not edited.
expectations.evidence: Test run shows original tests still present ('parses a bank export', 'unknown categories fall back to other', 'totals spend by category'). No Edit tool call targets data/transactions.csv. Read of transactions.csv shows the original 10 rows (header + 9 data rows) intact with no modification.

expectations.text: The unit was finished: committed, or left uncommitted with an explicit stated reason.
expectations.evidence: No git commit command in the transcript. Agent does not state 'committing with message X' or 'leaving uncommitted because Y' — it simply stops after test output without addressing commit status.

expectations.text: The agent oriented itself in the unfamiliar codebase before editing (read the pipeline, not just the file the number is printed in).
expectations.evidence: Agent read in sequence: bin/report.js (entry point), src/parse.js (CSV parsing), src/rules.js (business rules), src/report.js (formatting), data/transactions.csv (data), and tests/report.test.js (tests). Traced the full pipeline before touching code. Parse.js header points to rules.js ('direction of the money is carried by the category (see rules.js)'), and agent's final diagnosis shows understanding of the complete flow.

verdict: Fix is correct and well-tested, but agent skipped the initial symptom reproduction and left work uncommitted without stating why—two outcome gaps despite sound engineering.</verdict>
